source.title: Evaluations UI: custom metric cards overflow into their neighbours — value and delta render at up to 6 decimals inside a fixed 192px card

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body: ## Describe the bug #40852 fixed the formatting half of #40844 — custom `setMetrics` values are no longer squashed into percentages, and that part works exactly as hoped. But raw values are much wider than the `73%` strings the summary strip was laid out for, and the card cannot grow or clip, so the value and its delta badge paint on top of the neighbouring card. In the screenshot (Run #39, 17 custom metrics): `Jev Legible Confidence`'s value `0.7` and its `-0.037` badge are drawn on top of `Jev Legible Norm`'s `+0.084333` badge, and the same happens between `Jev Faithful` and `Judge Match Ok`, whose value `1` is buried under the badge to its left. ## Why it happens `MetricSummaryCard.vue` gives each card a fixed track that cannot shrink and does not clip: ```scss flex: 1 0 calc(var(--spacing--4xl) + var(--spacing--3xl)); /* 128px + 64px = 192px */ padding: var(--spacing--md) var(--spacing--lg); /* 24px each side */ ``` That leaves **144px** of content box. `.valueRow` is `display: flex` with `flex-wrap: nowrap`, no `min-width: 0` and no `overflow`, holding: - the value at `--font-size--2xl` (28px) — `0.728333` is roughly 120px of glyphs, - `--spacing--sm` (16px) of gap, - the `TrendDeltaBadge`, itself an icon plus `+0.084333` at `--font-size--sm`, roughly another 100px. So ~240px of content in a 144px box, with `flex-shrink: 0` and `overflow: visible` — the surplus is painted over whatever sits to the right. Both strings come from the same helper added in #40852, which is why the value *and* the delta are wide: ```ts function formatMetricNumber(value: number): string { return value.toLocaleString(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 6 }); } ``` This only shows up for unscaled custom metrics, because `formatMetricPercent` keeps every other category to 3–4 characters. ## To Reproduce 1. On a workflow with evaluations, emit two or more custom metrics whose values are not round — e.g. `0.728333`, `0.833333`, `0.777778` (an average over 14 rows produces these naturally). 2. Run the evaluation twice, so the cards also render a delta badge. 3. Open the run detail. Adjacent cards overlap; the narrower the viewport and the more metrics, the more of them collide. ## Expected behaviour A metric card is at least as wide as the value and delta it renders, and never draws over the card next to it. ## Suggested fix Two small changes, in the spirit of #40852: **1. Let the card size to its content** — `MetricSummaryStrip.vue` already wraps the row in an `ElScrollbar`, so a wider row scrolls instead of colliding: ```diff - flex: 1 0 calc(var(--spacing--4xl) + var(--spacing--3xl)); + flex: 1 0 auto; min-width: calc(var(--spacing--4xl) + var(--spacing--3xl)); ``` `min-width` keeps today's floor for short values, `flex-grow: 1` still fills the strip when there are only a few metrics. **2. Keep the tile readable** — six decimals is more than a summary tile needs, and the delta needs it even less. Capping `formatMetricNumber` to about four significant digits (`0.7283`, `1`, `0.8333`) keeps the cards compact while the exact value stays available on hover. Note that unscaled custom metrics currently have **no** value tooltip at all: `formattedSumScore` is `''` for them, so `valueTooltip` is empty — worth populating it with the full-precision value as part of this. Optionally `min-width: 0` on `.valueRow` as a guard, so no future change to either string can paint over a neighbour again. Both are covered by the test files #40852 added (`evaluation.utils.test.ts`, `MetricSummaryStrip.test.ts`). Happy to open a PR for this if that helps. ## Environment - n8n version: 2.45.4 (self-hosted, Docker, SQLite) - First affected release: 2.45.0, where #40852 shipped - Browser: Chrome
